recommendations.regimenLabel: Nimodipine + BP/pain control (with early aneurysm securing)
steps: EMERGENCY — resuscitate (ABC), neurosurgery / stroke team immediately.
CT angiography to localise aneurysm; secure aneurysm early (endovascular coiling or clipping).
Nimodipine 60 mg PO q4h to reduce vasospasm-related deficits.
Control pain and BP (avoid extreme swings); bed rest, analgesia, antiemetics.
Monitor for hydrocephalus, rebleeding, vasospasm, hyponatraemia.

drugRefs.why: Reduces delayed cerebral ischaemia from vasospasm and improves neurological outcome; standard for 21 days.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Subarachnoid Haemorrhage
AHA/ASA Guidelines for the Management of Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Haemorrhage
Neurocritical Care Society — Critical Care Management of SAH

drugRefs.dose: 10-20 mg IV bolus, then infusion titrated
drugRefs.why: Titratable control of hypertension before the aneurysm is secured, avoiding extreme swings.
First-line analgesia for the severe headache; opioids may be added if needed.
Controls nausea/vomiting and reduces straining that could raise ICP or provoke rebleeding.

refs: AHA/ASA Guidelines for the Management of Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Haemorrhage
Neurocritical Care Society — Critical Care Management of SAH

decision.label: Secure aneurysm early + nimodipine + BP control

confirm: Sudden thunderclap (worst-ever) headache ± neck stiffness, photophobia, transient LOC. Non-contrast CT head; LP for xanthochromia if CT negative and high suspicion.
